newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket - West Indies to discipline Lara for outburst.
newsitem.headline: Cricket - West Indies to discipline Lara for outburst.

text.p: West Indies batsman Brian Lara, who stormed into the Australia dressing room to protest against his dismissal in the second test, will be disciplined for his actions, tour manager Clive Lloyd said on Thurday.
West Indies management have already apologised for Lara's heated outburst during a confrontion with Australia coach Geoff Marsh at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Tuesday.
"I think he (Lara) realises he stepped out of line and we'll deal with that in-house. We have ways of doing it," Lloyd said. "Brian is vice-captain and he has got to play by the rules."
But Lloyd, the former West Indies captain, did not detail the disciplinary action that would be taken against team vice-captain Lara, other than saying it would be "in-house".

Lara, who holds the record for the highest score in test and first-class cricket, was infuriated by his second innings dismissal and took his complaint to the opposition dressing room. West Indies lost the match by 124 runs to go two-nil down in the five-test series.
Lara, who refused to comment on the incident during training on Thursday, was dismissed for one when he edged a catch to wicketkeeper Ian Healy on the fifth and final day of the test.
Healy tumbled forward to take the catch but television replays raised doubt as to whether the ball carried.
Australia captain Mark Taylor praised Lloyd's handling of the incident, saying: "The West Indies management have done the right thing and apologised to us.
"As far as I'm concerned one incident with one individual is not going to sour relationships."
On his arrival in Australia last month, Lara said he was determined to avoid a repeat of his experience on West Indies' tour of England last year when he was fined for misconduct.
Healy said he would not approach Lara to settle any possible differences between them.
"If he wants to come to me so we can put things back straight, I would have no problem with that," Healy said.
In their immediate post-match interviews both Taylor and Healy said the catch was valid, Walsh refused to do likewise.
Asked about the incident, Walsh said: "Everyone saw it and I'd rather not comment".
Australia and West Indies have experienced a fierce rivalry over recent series, leading to several unsavoury incidents.
Four years ago, Healy stumped Lara in the Brisbane test but television replays showed the wicketkeeper did not have the ball in his gloves when he removed the bails.
